events.title: George Washington issues the first presidential veto
events.summary: It is the first veto in US history.
events.description: On April 5, 1792, George Washington issued the first presidential veto in US history.
events.notificationBody: In 1792, George Washington issued the first presidential veto in US history.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 5

events.title: Chile wins the Battle of Maipu
events.summary: The victory over Spain secures Chile's independence movement.
events.description: On April 5, 1818, Chile's independence movement won a decisive victory over Spain at the Battle of Maipu.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 5

events.title: Chile declares war on Peru and Bolivia
events.summary: The declaration begins the War of the Pacific.
events.description: On April 5, 1879, Chile declared war on Peru and Bolivia, beginning the War of the Pacific.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 5

events.title: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar becomes the NBA's top scorer
events.summary: He passes Wilt Chamberlain's career points total.
events.description: On April 5, 1984, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar surpassed Wilt Chamberlain as the all-time leading scorer in the National Basketball Association.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 5

events.title: Bette Davis is born
events.summary: The film actress is born in Lowell, Massachusetts.
events.description: On April 5, 1908, the American film actress Bette Davis was born in Lowell, Massachusetts.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 5

events.title: The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens
events.dateNote: Gregorian date. Greece then used the Julian calendar, in which the Games opened on March 25.
events.summary: Athletes from 12 countries gather in Greece.
events.description: On April 6, 1896, the first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens, with as many as 280 athletes, all men, from 12 countries.
events.notificationBody: In 1896, the first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 6
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Athens 1896 Olympic Games

events.title: ABBA wins Eurovision with 'Waterloo'
events.summary: The Swedish group's victory launches its international career.
events.description: On April 6, 1974, the Swedish group ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest with the song 'Waterloo.'

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 6

events.title: The United States declares war on Germany
events.summary: The US enters World War I.
events.description: On April 6, 1917, the United States declared war on Germany, entering World War I.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 6

events.title: The Battle of Shiloh begins in Tennessee
events.summary: Union and Confederate armies clash in southwestern Tennessee.
events.description: On April 6, 1862, Union troops clashed with Confederates at the Battle of Shiloh in southwestern Tennessee.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 6

events.title: The first Tony Awards are presented
events.summary: Broadway's awards are handed out for the first time.
events.description: On April 6, 1947, the Tony Awards were presented for the first time.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 6

events.title: The World Health Organization is established
events.summary: The UN health agency is born; the date becomes World Health Day.
events.description: On April 7, 1948, the World Health Organization, a specialized agency of the United Nations based in Geneva, was formally established. The date is marked each year as World Health Day.
events.notificationBody: In 1948, the World Health Organization was established; the date is now World Health Day.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 7
Encyclopaedia Britannica - World Health Organization

events.title: The Rwandan genocide begins
events.summary: Prime Minister Agathe Uwilingiyimana is assassinated.
events.description: On April 7, 1994, Rwandan Prime Minister Agathe Uwilingiyimana was assassinated by Hutu soldiers, marking the beginning of the Rwandan genocide.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 7

events.title: Henry Ford dies
events.summary: The pioneer of assembly-line car making dies at 83.
events.description: On April 7, 1947, Henry Ford, who pioneered assembly-line methods at the Ford Motor Company, died at age 83.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 7

events.title: Billie Holiday is born in Philadelphia
events.summary: One of the greatest jazz singers is born.
events.description: On April 7, 1915, Billie Holiday, one of the greatest American jazz singers, was born in Philadelphia.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 7

events.title: NASA launches 2001 Mars Odyssey
events.summary: The spacecraft heads for Mars.
events.description: On April 7, 2001, NASA launched the 2001 Mars Odyssey spacecraft, which reached Mars in October and sent back photos and data.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 7

events.title: Hank Aaron hits his 715th home run
events.summary: He breaks Babe Ruth's career record.
events.description: On April 8, 1974, Hank Aaron hit his 715th career home run, breaking Babe Ruth's record, which had stood since 1935.
events.notificationBody: In 1974, Hank Aaron hit his 715th home run, breaking Babe Ruth's record.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 8

events.title: The Venus de Milo is found on Melos
events.summary: The ancient marble statue turns up in pieces.
events.description: On April 8, 1820, the Venus de Milo, an ancient marble statue thought to represent the goddess Aphrodite, was found in pieces on the Aegean island of Melos. It is now in the Louvre.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 8
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Venus de Milo

events.title: Pablo Picasso dies
events.summary: One of the 20th century's most influential artists dies at 91.
events.description: On April 8, 1973, Pablo Picasso, one of the most influential artists of the 20th century, died in France at age 91.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 8

events.title: The Seventeenth Amendment is ratified
events.summary: Voters gain the right to elect US senators directly.
events.description: On April 8, 1913, the Seventeenth Amendment to the US Constitution, providing for the direct election of senators by the voters of each state, was ratified.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 8

events.title: Kofi Annan is born
events.summary: The seventh UN secretary-general is born.
events.description: On April 8, 1938, Kofi Annan, who became the seventh secretary-general of the United Nations, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 8

events.title: Robert E. Lee surrenders at Appomattox Court House
events.summary: The Army of Northern Virginia surrenders to Ulysses S. Grant.
events.description: On April 9, 1865, Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Union General Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, Virginia, effectively ending the American Civil War in Virginia.
events.notificationBody: In 1865, Robert E. Lee surrendered his army to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 9
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Battle of Appomattox Court House

events.title: Marian Anderson sings at the Lincoln Memorial
events.summary: The contralto performs for an Easter Sunday crowd of 75,000.
events.description: On April 9, 1939, the contralto Marian Anderson gave a concert to an Easter Sunday crowd of 75,000 at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 9

events.title: Winston Churchill becomes an honorary US citizen
events.summary: An act of Congress confers the honor.
events.description: On April 9, 1963, an act of the US Congress conferred honorary US citizenship on Sir Winston Churchill.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 9

events.title: Paul Robeson is born in Princeton
events.summary: The singer, actor and activist is born.
events.description: On April 9, 1898, Paul Robeson, the singer, actor and political activist, was born in Princeton, New Jersey.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 9

events.title: La Salle claims the Mississippi basin for France
events.summary: He names the region Louisiana.
events.description: On April 9, 1682, the French explorer Rene-Robert Cavelier, sieur de La Salle, claimed the Mississippi River basin for France and named it Louisiana.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 9

events.title: The Good Friday Agreement is signed
events.summary: The peace deal for Northern Ireland is reached.
events.description: On April 10, 1998, the Good Friday Agreement (also called the Belfast Agreement), a peace accord for Northern Ireland, was signed.
events.notificationTitle: A peace deal for Northern Ireland
events.notificationBody: In 1998, the Good Friday Agreement for peace in Northern Ireland was signed.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 10
Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: March 21

events.title: The Great Gatsby is published
events.summary: F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel appears.
events.description: On April 10, 1925, F. Scott Fitzgerald published his novel The Great Gatsby.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 10

events.title: Emiliano Zapata is killed in an ambush
events.summary: The Mexican revolutionary leader is shot dead.
events.description: On April 10, 1919, the Mexican revolutionary leader Emiliano Zapata was ambushed and shot dead.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 10

events.title: Astronomers release the first image of a black hole
events.summary: The picture shows the shadow of a black hole for the first time.
events.description: On April 10, 2019, astronomers released the first image of a black hole.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 10

events.title: Walter Hunt patents the safety pin
events.summary: He later sells the rights for $400.
events.description: On April 10, 1849, Walter Hunt patented the safety pin in the United States. He later sold his rights to it for $400.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 10

events.title: Apollo 13 is launched toward the Moon
events.summary: An oxygen tank failure later forces the crew to abandon the landing.
events.description: On April 11, 1970, Apollo 13 was launched from Cape Kennedy, Florida, with James Lovell, John Swigert and Fred Haise. An oxygen tank failure forced them to abandon the Moon landing, and they returned safely on April 17.
events.notificationBody: In 1970, Apollo 13 launched for the Moon; an oxygen tank failure later forced a return.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 11
NASA - Apollo 13

events.title: Truman relieves General Douglas MacArthur of command
events.summary: The president removes the commander of UN forces in Korea.
events.description: On April 11, 1951, US President Harry S. Truman relieved General Douglas MacArthur of his command of United Nations and US forces during the Korean War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 11

events.title: The trial of Adolf Eichmann begins in Jerusalem
events.summary: The Nazi official faces judgment in Israel.
events.description: On April 11, 1961, the trial of the Nazi official Adolf Eichmann began in Jerusalem. It ended eight months later with a death sentence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 11

events.title: Kurt Vonnegut dies
events.summary: The author of Slaughterhouse-Five dies at 84.
events.description: On April 11, 2007, Kurt Vonnegut, the author of satirical novels such as Slaughterhouse-Five (1969), died at age 84.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 11

events.title: Andrew Wiles is born in Cambridge
events.summary: The mathematician who proved Fermat's last theorem is born.
events.description: On April 11, 1953, the English mathematician Andrew Wiles, who devised a proof of Fermat's last theorem, was born in Cambridge.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 11

events.title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
events.summary: Vostok 1 carries him once around Earth.
events.description: On April 12, 1961, the Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space, making one orbit of Earth in 1 hour 29 minutes aboard Vostok 1.
events.notificationBody: In 1961, Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth aboard Vostok 1, the first human in space.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 12
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Yuri Gagarin

events.title: Confederate guns open fire on Fort Sumter
events.summary: The attack begins the American Civil War.
events.description: On April 12, 1861, Confederate guns opened fire on Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina, beginning the American Civil War. The Union garrison under Major Robert Anderson surrendered after a 34-hour bombardment.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 12
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Fort Sumter

events.title: Jonas Salk's polio vaccine is declared safe and effective
events.summary: Results of a huge field trial clear the vaccine for use.
events.description: On April 12, 1955, the results of a two-year field trial involving nearly two million children were announced, showing Jonas Salk's inactivated polio vaccine to be safe and effective. It was released for use in the United States that day.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 12
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Jonas Salk

events.title: NASA launches the first space shuttle, Columbia
events.summary: The reusable spacecraft makes its first flight.
events.description: On April 12, 1981, NASA launched the first space shuttle, Columbia, designed to orbit Earth and carry people and cargo.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 12

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt dies
events.summary: The US president dies at age 63 while in office.
events.description: On April 12, 1945, US President Franklin D. Roosevelt died at age 63.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: April 12
